page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical cores, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a local 2880 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong computational and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU performance. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read and write speeds ranking in the top 10% of tested configurations. Multi-core stress-ng performance, Passmark CPU scores, and software compilation benchmarks fall within the top 25%. For data processing, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also reach top-tier performance levels.

This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and large-scale data processing. It demonstrates strong capabilities in Redis SET operations and static web serving, both ranking in the top 25%. While the CPU supports advanced vector extensions like AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI, it lacks AMX instructions, and its lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training. However, for CPU-based LLM inference, it delivers strong text generation speeds on medium 7B models, though performance drops to average levels for larger 70B models.

Lacking a dedicated GPU, it is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large databases, and CPU-based inference tasks.
